name: holo-card

frames.best_why: Card faces the camera squarely, so the full rainbow foil and the photo underneath both read clearly.

tagline: Rainbow foil rings shift across a photo as the card tilts.
summary: A collectible-style card holding a photo, covered edge to edge in a shimmering holographic pattern of concentric rings that moves and changes colour as you tilt it or move the pointer across it.
appearance: A portrait, rounded-corner card centred on a black stage, with a photo showing under a dense overlay of repeating concentric ring motifs in shifting rainbow foil: reds, blues, greens and gold.
behaviour: Moving the pointer across the card tilts it in 3D toward the cursor and slides the light, so the foil pattern and colours flow across the surface. Left alone, it drifts gently on its own while a soft shadow tracks the tilt beneath it.
demo_content: A portrait photo of a smiling woman with shoulder-length dark hair against an indoor background.
search_phrases: card that tilts with the mouse
use_when: A product, profile or collectible should feel like a premium card whose foil reacts to the pointer.
avoid_when: Relies on WebGL and keeps a shader running while idle, so it drains low-power devices and is heavy for many cards.
customise: Image, back image, alt, preset, intensity, scale, edge sparkle, frame, glare, foil colour, width, radius, tilt and hover scale are props. The eight foil patterns are fixed in the shader.
weight_why: A full fragment shader redraws every frame, with spring physics running continuously while idle.

a11y.note: Without a back image the card is a non-focusable image and tilting is pointer-only; reduced motion is respected.

issues: At the default intensity the dense foil rings largely bury the photo they are meant to decorate.
polish_why: Rich, convincing foil and tilt; the shader pattern is dense enough to obscure the image.
